To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the structural response of reinforced ultra high performance concrete can be predicted by considering the bond slip laws, the strain compatibility, the formation and opening and closing of cracks and the stress redistribution.
the bond behaviour of reinforcing bars in UHPFRC is significantly different from that in normal concrete and the analytical approach is capable of predicting the structural behaviour of the UHPF.
the structural behaviour of UHPFRE is strongly influenced by the bond-slip behaviour of the reinforcing bars.
In summary, our research is concerned with

(i) The structural response of reinforced ultra high performance concrete, (ii) The structural response and the bond behaviour of UHPFRCC, (iii) The development of a numerical model to predict the structural response of reinforced and unreinforced UHPFRC.
the structural behaviour of UHPFR C combined with various grades of reinforcing steel.

the following topics: (i) the structural behaviour of UHPFFC with various types and ratios reinforcement; (ii) the bond-slip behaviour between reinforcement and UHPFRC; (iii) the structural behaviour in bending of composite members combining UHPFRC layers and concrete beams; (iv) the structural behaviour under combined loading of composite members combining a UHPFRC column and a reinforced concrete beam.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the structural behaviour of a UHPFRC member with reinforcing steel bars is governed by the mechanical properties of the UHPFEC and the bond behaviour of reinforcing steel bars.
the use of UHPF RC with bar reinforcement is a promising approach for the structural rehabilitation of existing reinforced concrete structures.

the addition of reinforcement bars to UHPFRC improves the structural response and that the mechanical properties of the composite material are influenced by the mechanical properties of UHPFBC, the type and ratio of reinforcement and the bond behaviour.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
reinforced UHPFRCS are able to achieve a high level of ductility and energy dissipation capacity, even with the use of low grade reinforcement steel.
the use of UHPFCR in composite construction is feasible and that the structural response of reinforced and plain UHPFCR can be predicted with a reasonable accuracy.
the structural performance is strongly influenced by the type and the ratio of reinforcement.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the bond slip law of the reinforcement is the key to predict the structural response of reinforced concrete.
reinforced UHPFCR can be designed with a simple approach, based on the bond behaviour of the reinforcement and the strain compatibility between concrete and reinforcement.
the bond between steel and UHPFRC is not a limiting factor for the structural behaviour of UHPFR.
